summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease and a history of multiple transplants was admitted for removal of her peritoneal dialysis catheter due to inadequate volume clearance as a rapid transporter. She had transitioned to hemodialysis and elected to have the catheter removed. The procedure was performed on 2193-08-06 without complications. Postoperatively, she was started on a heparin drip for anticoagulation bridging due to her mechanical mitral valve. Warfarin was resumed the following day, and her INR rose from 2.1 to 3.0 by discharge. She tolerated diet, had a bowel movement with assistance, and completed a hemodialysis session with 2 liters of fluid removed. She remained stable, alert, and ambulatory throughout her stay. She was discharged home on her prior medications, including warfarin 6 mg daily, with instructions to follow up with the coagulation clinic and resume outpatient hemodialysis.
problems: Mechanical complication due to peritoneal dialysis catheter
Heart valve replaced by other means
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Kidney dialysis as the cause of abnormal reaction of patient, or of later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of procedure
